analysis: Docs-only change to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (date bump line 3; new Swift-only `detail` field on model_autopilot_status at head line 854; new Swift-only `hold_seconds` on model_autopilot at head line 1208; further changed ranges 1355-1380 and 1470-1472 are outside the supplied units). No executable code, keys, attestation, or routing logic changed in the supplied evidence, so no concrete regression is identified. Security-relevant observations for later passes: (1) `hold_seconds` is described as a placement hold that keeps a loaded model out of LRU eviction and idle unload; it is bounded 0...86400, honoured only by providers reporting `placement_holds`, and is coordinator-sent, so a compromised or abusive coordinator could pin memory. The coordinator is trusted in the threat model, and the doc states other operations may still unload it. Still, the Swift implementation (ModelAutopilot.swift) should enforce the bound and the invalid_command rule when load_model_id is absent; that was not supplied. (2) `detail` on model_autopilot_status carries busy reasons, sent only with consent, with older coordinators ignoring it; it contains no prompt content per the doc, but the implementation should be confirmed to emit only closed reason strings, not free text, so as not to leak consumer data (A-001). It is described as diagnostic and not an authorization or capacity signal. (3) Existing guarantees (model_not_selected allowlist, expiry bounds, command ID reuse rejection) appear unchanged. Retained T-041 cache text is unchanged by this PR. The excerpt of the patch is truncated and the 1355-1380 and 1470-1472 ranges were not visible, so any security-relevant doc changes there are unreviewed.
